claims.text: Development that meets present needs without undermining future generations' ability to meet their own needs.

claims.text: Sustainable development connects present livelihoods and well-being with continued resource availability and environmental quality. An immediate output gain is insufficient if it damages the capacity to meet future needs.

claims.text: Renewable resources can replenish on human timescales under suitable conditions, but can still be depleted by overuse. Non-renewable resources have finite stocks that are not replaced on those timescales.

claims.text: Conservation can limit extraction, reduce waste and protect regeneration or ecosystems. A resource being renewable does not remove the need to manage its use.

claims.text: Sustainable agriculture maintains farming and the resources on which it depends; sustainable development is the broader principle covering livelihoods, services and other dimensions as well as farming.

claims.text: Responsible consumption and production concern how resources are obtained, used and discarded, including waste prevention, reuse, repair and suitable recycling.

claims.text: Compare alternatives by the stated aim, their full resource use and practical constraints. A reusable product reduces disposable waste when it is used sufficiently and the cleaning or maintenance arrangements are suitable.

claims.text: Preventing avoidable material loss can reduce demand for new inputs and disposal, while meeting the same need; a higher initial cost or missing maintenance capacity may limit adoption.

claims.text: The United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) organise international development ambitions for 2030. The saved 2022 examination figure shows examples including No Poverty, Zero Hunger, Good Health and Well-being, Clean Water and Sanitation, Decent Work and Economic Growth, and Responsible Consumption and Production. The syllabus specifically names SDG 12. Sustainable development can be considered through linked economic, social and environmental pillars; a goal may contribute to more than one, so do not force every goal into only one pillar. Progress in one area can help another, but trade-offs still need a judgement about present and future needs.

claims.text: SDG 12 concerns responsible consumption and production. Reusing suitable fabric offcuts can reduce the need for new material and reduce waste. SDG 8 concerns decent work and economic growth; a viable product can connect to this goal when it supports decent paid work. Goals can interact, but a local action does not by itself establish progress against a global goal.
